digest.top_line: ESTRO Delphi locks prostate SBRT at 36.25Gy/5fx and votes 100% against elective pelvic nodal RT alongside it.
digest.tldr: Prostate carried the day, both readings pushing toward less treatment. ESTRO's panel fixes a 5fx dose and rules out elective nodal coverage and rectal spacers, while capping SBRT at ISUP 2-3 / cT2c / PSA <20. ProtecT's cribriform re-review argues the 87% cribriform-negative GG2 pts track GG1 for 15yr metastases, with no significant radical-treatment benefit.

sites.intro: Two reads on who gets radical local therapy and how much: a consensus framework for delivering SBRT and a biopsy-morphology argument for withholding treatment entirely.

studies.name: ProtecT Secondary Analysis (Cribriform Morphology)
studies.tldr: Cribriform-negative grade group 2 carried the same 15yr metastasis risk as GG1, and radical treatment showed no significant benefit in that 87%.
details: 🔍 Secondary analysis of ProtecT: centrally re-reviewed biopsy slides from 712 of 1,643 randomized pts
🔍 Grades re-scored to 2019 ISUP (original trial used 2005); regrading did not shift group balance
📊 Cribriform-positive on biopsy in roughly 13% of the reviewed cohort; 87% cribriform-negative
📊 In cribriform-negative pts, early radical treatment gave no statistically significant reduction in 15yr metastases vs active monitoring
📊 Consistent across both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses (per-protocol accounts for crossover)
📊 On multivariable Cox (ITT), cribriform-negative grade group 2 had the same long-term metastasis risk as Gleason 6 / GG1
🔗 Frames the ProtecT paradox: 15yr PCa-specific mortality was extremely low (over 3% quoted in source) and equal across arms, while radical treatment cut metastases overall
🔗 EAU already advises against active surveillance with any cribriform at diagnostic biopsy; ISUP and GUPS require binary cribriform reporting
⚠️ Cribriform status was not a randomization characteristic, so these are non-randomized subgroups within a randomized trial
⚠️ Only 43% of the randomized cohort had slides available; source notes a trend to higher cribriform prevalence in the RT + neoadjuvant ADT arm, attributed to chance
⚠️ No effect sizes (HR, CI, p) reported in source text for the cribriform-negative or cribriform-positive comparisons: this is a video interview transcript, not the paper

verdict.rationale: Post-hoc subgroup on 43% of randomized pts with slides available; cribriform was not a stratification factor and no effect sizes appear in the source.
verdict.audience: PSA-screened clinically localized prostate cancer, GG1-2, biopsy cribriform…

studies.significance: The RT-relevant read is patient selection, not technique: cribriform-negative GG2 behaved like GG1 for 15yr metastasis, and radical treatment (surgery or RT with 3-6mo neoadjuvant ADT) showed no significant metastasis reduction in that 87%. Effect sizes are not in the source text. Cribriform status is already a required biopsy report field, so it is available at consult.
studies.monday_clinic: In a PSA-screened GG2 patient whose biopsy is reported cribriform-negative, this supports monitoring as a discussable option rather than automatic definitive RT or surgery; it does not speak to cribriform-positive disease, where EAU already advises against surveillance.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Secondary analysis of the **ProtecT** randomized trial (active monitoring vs surgery vs radiotherapy with 3-6mo neoadjuvant ADT). Central pathology re-review of available biopsy slides, analyzed both **intention-to-treat** and **per-protocol** (accounting for crossover).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: PSA-screened men with clinically localized prostate cancer. Slides were located for **712 of 1,643** randomized participants; age, PSA and revised Gleason score did not differ significantly across the three groups in the reviewed subset.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary outcome of this analysis: metastases at 15-year median follow-up**, by binary cribriform status. Grades re-scored under **2019 ISUP** criteria rather than the trial-era 2005 criteria.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **Roughly 13%** of the reviewed cohort was cribriform-positive. In the cribriform-negative **87%**, early radical treatment produced **no statistically significant reduction** in 15yr metastases vs active monitoring, in both ITT and per-protocol. Multivariable Cox: cribriform-negative **GG2 carried the same metastasis risk as GG1**. No effect sizes are reported in the source text.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PSA-screened, clinically localized, predominantly low- and intermediate-grade prostate cancer with biopsy cribriform status assessable. Does not represent high-risk, cribriform-positive, or MRI-targeted-biopsy cohorts, where the guideline position already differs.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Slide centralization is incomplete and ongoing, so 931 of the randomized cohort contributed no pathology. The source is a video interview transcript that stops mid-sentence before the cribriform-positive outcomes, so the group that actually drives the guideline question is not quantified here.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This is a selection question, not a dose question: in the cribriform-negative 87%, radiotherapy with 3-6mo neoadjuvant ADT showed no significant 15yr metastasis reduction over monitoring, and GG2 tracked with GG1. Cribriform status is already reported on the biopsy, so it can be read at the RT consult before committing to definitive treatment.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Binary cribriform status is a routinely reported biopsy variable that separated metastatic risk here, and EAU already uses it to gate surveillance. The RT arm carried 3-6mo neoadjuvant ADT, so the treated comparator was not RT alone. No effect sizes appear in the source text.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: For a cribriform-negative GG2 biopsy, radical prostatectomy showed no significant 15yr metastasis advantage over active monitoring in this analysis, and that grade behaved like GG1. The read supports discussing surveillance in that group, while cribriform-positive disease remains a separate conversation.

open_questions: Metastasis outcomes in the cribriform-positive 13% not reported in source
Does cribriform status justify treatment in grade group 2?
Will 20-year ProtecT follow-up confirm the grade group 2 finding?

studies.name: ESTRO Prostate SBRT Consensus Recommendations
studies.tldr: ESTRO Delphi consensus: 36.25Gy/5fx (40Gy to 95% CTV) standard, 100% against elective pelvic nodal RT with prostate SBRT.

details.text: 📊 Q1 panel votes on SBRT as standard treatment outside a trial, by risk feature
📊 Consensus questions where the panel split or agreed against a common practice

rows: Elective pelvic nodal RT with prostate SBRT (Q6)

details.text: 📐 Dose: 36.25Gy/5fx of 7.25Gy to 95% PTV, with 40Gy to 95% of prostate CTV

details: 🔍 Volume cut-offs quantified where the panel used them: median IPSS cut-off 17 (range 10-20), median prostate volume 90cc (range 70-150cc), median post-BPH-surgery wait 6mo (range 2-12mo)
🔍 Margin-dependent motion management: PTV ≥5mm needs pre-treatment CBCT/fiducial matching (79%, 11 votes); at <5mm, 71% (10 votes) wanted added intra-fraction tracking but no consensus was declared

details.text: 🔗 Seminal vesicles: omit in low-risk; PACE trials included proximal 1cm for all, proximal 2cm to 30Gy/5fx for Gleason 4+3 or NCCN high-risk
🔗 NRG-GU005 (ASTRO 2025 preliminary) reported lower toxicity with 36.25Gy/5fx but a slightly higher 3-year biochemical relapse rate
⚠️ Panel is 15 people (11 rad oncs, 3 physicists, 1 RTT) from 9 European countries; several 100% figures rest on 12-14 votes

details: ⚠️ High-risk evidence is thin: HYPO-RT-PC is the only phase III reporting oncologic outcomes in high-risk pts and they were 11% of accrual; PACE-C has toxicity only

⚠️ Urethral constraint flagged as possibly too permissive: PACE-B V42 <50% carries an explicit note that hotspots should be avoided; a post-hoc PACE-B analysis found no association between urinary substructure dose and late toxicity
⚠️ Tables 1-3 (target volume parameters, OOI dose guidance, IGRT-by-margin grid) arrived with uncertain row-to-value association in source extraction, so per-row constraints are not reproduced here
studies.significance: Two votes bind practice hardest: 100% against elective pelvic nodal irradiation with prostate SBRT outside a trial, and 85% against rectal spacers, both areas where department habit often runs ahead of evidence. The dose anchor is dual-level (36.25Gy/5fx to 95% PTV with 40Gy to 95% CTV), so a single-prescription plan is not what PACE-B delivered.
studies.monday_clinic: In ISUP 2-3, cT1c-cT2c, PSA <20 ng/mL localised prostate cancer, this supports five-fraction SBRT with prostate-only targeting and no spacer; it does not extend to cT3b, ISUP 5, or pts needing pelvic nodal coverage, where the panel voted 0%.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: ESTRO clinical practice consensus. A task force drafted 'how to' recommendations, then a **15-member expert panel** (11 radiation oncologists, 3 medical physicists, 1 RTT) from **nine European countries** reviewed them. **Two Delphi rounds** of web survey covered ten multiple-choice questions on areas of controversy, with final adjustments made at ESTRO 2025 Vienna.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: No efficacy endpoint. Agreement thresholds followed APCCC: **consensus ≥75%**, **strong consensus ≥90%**. Votes are reported per question with abstentions counted separately, so denominators shift between 12 and 14.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **36.25 Gy in 5 fractions of 7.25 Gy to 95% of the PTV, with 40 Gy to 95% of the prostate CTV**, is the standard prescription; **42.7 Gy in 7 fractions of 6.1 Gy** (HYPO-RT-PC) is the alternative. MRI co-registration with T2-weighted sequences is strongly recommended for contouring, planning CT slice thickness ≤2 mm from L3/L4 to external genitalia. Margins of **5 mm** are standard, **4 mm** in hypo-FLAME and MIRAGE, and **2-3 mm** only with integrated motion management.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **Strong consensus** landed on ISUP 2-3 / cT1c-cT2c / PSA <20 as the standard SBRT population, on bladder-bowel preparation, on guideline-concordant ADT independent of fractionation, and on **not** irradiating pelvic nodes electively. **No consensus** on a prostate volume cut-off or on prophylactic medications. Treatment frequency: QOD or more protracted preferred over QD given low-grade toxicity signals, with no oncologic detriment demonstrated from protraction.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents localised ISUP 2-3, cT1c-cT2c, PSA <20 ng/mL prostate cancer treated with gantry-based five-fraction SBRT. Does not represent cT3b or ISUP 5 disease, pts requiring pelvic nodal coverage, or proton-based SBRT, which the panel places outside standard of care.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: European-only panel of 15 with abstentions on most questions, so a 100% figure can rest on 12 votes. Dose constraints are drawn almost entirely from **PACE-B** with one hypo-FLAME borrow, and the document itself flags the PACE-B urethral V42 <50% constraint as possibly too permissive. The high-risk and post-BPH-surgery guidance is expert opinion, not trial-derived.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Open dose questions are named rather than settled: NRG-GU005 preliminary data at ASTRO 2025 showed lower toxicity with the reduced 36.25 Gy dose but a slightly higher 3-year biochemical relapse rate, cause unexplained. Focal GTV escalation >40-50 Gy/5fx for high-risk (NCT05705921, NCT06330909) and de-escalation to 30 Gy/5fx for non-suspicious prostate in lower risk (NCT05709496) are both still in trials. Online adaptive RT is feasible but its benefit over non-adaptive delivery is unestablished, and a risk analysis put daily contouring as the highest-risk failure mode.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The prescription is two-level, not one: 36.25Gy/5fx to 95% PTV **and** 40Gy to 95% of the CTV, so a homogeneous single-level plan diverges from PACE-B. The panel voted 100% against elective pelvic nodal RT with prostate SBRT outside a trial and 85% against rectal spacers, and required intra-fraction tracking only once PTV margin drops below 5 mm.

open_questions: Cause of higher 3-year biochemical relapse with reduced 36.25 Gy dose
Whether focal GTV dose escalation improves outcome in high-risk disease
Clinical benefit of online adaptive RT over non-adaptive prostate SBRT
